items.title: 1 Corinthians 10:1–2 explicitly compares Israel’s Red Sea & cloud crossing (Exodus 14) to baptism ("baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea")
items.summary: Paul writes that Israel’s fathers were "under the cloud, and all passed through the sea (διὰ τῆς θαλάσσης διῆλθον), and were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea (εἰς τὸν Μωϋσῆν ἐβαπτίσαντο ἐν τῇ νεφέλῃ καὶ ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ)," calling these events examples/types (τύποι G5179 in 1 Cor 10:6). This separates the historical Exodus 13–14 event from Paul’s later NT typological interpretation.
limitations: Explicit NT authorial typology by Paul (1 Cor 10:1–6); Exodus 14 itself narrates a historical deliverance without using ritual washing/baptism terminology.
Do not infer that every narrative detail of Exodus 14 is an allegory or fixed symbol of Christian baptism beyond Paul’s explicit comparison (cloud, sea passage, deliverance under Moses).

items.title: Stronger biblical wordplay: Genesis 2:5–7 juxtaposes אָדָם (adam H0120) and אֲדָמָה (adamah H0127, ground) sharing consonants א-ד-ם
items.summary: Genesis 2:5–7 exhibits direct biblical paronomasia: there was no human (אָדָם) to work the ground (אֲדָמָה), and God formed the human (הָאָדָם) of dust from the ground (מִן־הָאֲדָמָה, Gen 2:7; cf. Gen 3:19). Unlike אָדָם/דָּם, both share the full triliteral sequence א-ד-ם and are juxtaposed explicitly in the Hebrew narrative.
limitations: Gen 2:7 establishes אָדָם ↔ אֲדָמָה (human ↔ ground), contrasting sharply with the weaker modern/midrashic אָדָם ↔ דָּם pairing.

items.title: Genesis 1 creation (Spirit over waters, light, sevenfold completion) and Revelation 4–5 & 21–22 (throne of Creator, seven Spirits, new creation)
items.summary: Genesis 1 opens with God creating heavens/earth, the Spirit/wind (רוּחַ אֱלֹהִים) hovering over the waters (v.2), light out of darkness (v.3), and sevenfold completion (Gen 2:1–3). Revelation 4:5–11 explicitly worships the Creator ("you created all things" v.11) before the seven Spirits/lamps (v.5), while Revelation 21:1,5 & 22:1–5 announce the "new heaven and new earth" with light, throne, river of water of life, and tree of life.
limitations: Rev 4:11 and Rev 21–22 explicitly recall Creation theology and Eden motifs, whereas connecting Gen 1:2’s singular Spirit directly to Rev 4:5’s "seven Spirits" passes through Isa 11:2 / Zech 4:2–10 rather than an explicit Gen 1 citation inside Rev 4:5.
